## 42ccd1ff25f3

### Finding: fixed-anchor Voronoi shortcut

The generator always puts its three seeds at `(1,1)`, `(1,w-2)`, and
`(h-2,3)`. Across 600 sampled normal generations (200 per difficulty band), all
600 used exactly those positions. A rival that reads the three colors in raster
order but computes the Voronoi partition from those three virtual anchors—while
preserving nonzero input cells—matched the intended nearest-seed rule on all
600 generated inputs. It ignores the actual seed coordinates, so it does not
learn the authority’s general rule.

A canonical counterexample is:

```text
00000000
00000050
00000000
00000000
00700000
00000000
00000020
00000000
```

Protected Racket executes the canonical rule as:

```text
77755555
77755555
77775555
77777555
77777022
77770222
77702222
77702222
```

The fixed-anchor rival gives:

```text
55557777
55557757
55557777
55520777
55722077
22222200
22222222
22222222
```

The generator should randomize all seed positions subject to separation and
non-collinearity, include different seed counts when lawful, and make ties occur
in varied locations. Its `self_check` should validate geometric properties
rather than require one exact anchor set.
